newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total says Caspian Sea studies completed.
newsitem.headline: Total says Caspian Sea studies completed.

text.p: French oil group Total SA said on Tuesday that exploration studies by a consortium in the Caspian Sea, begun in December 1993, had been completed.
It said the consortium had the right to select 12 blocks where a series of drills would be launched after the signing of a production-sharing agreement with Kazakhstan.
The consortium includes Kazakh group KCS, Total, Italy's Agip, British Gas, Mobil, Shell and a grouping of British Petroleum and Statoil.
In a statement Total described the works as "the most important seismic studies in the world".
Kazakh officials said last week that the country may need $150 billion to tap its huge oil reserves and that production-sharing agreements may be signed this summer.
